title: Silvermist Renewal & Capacity Strategy Review
summary: Customer approaching contract renewal; evaluating modest committed uplift plus burst capacity and onboarding EU region. Security team wants audit/logging and KMS; platform team wants a staging runbook and latency SLAs. Agreed to pilot 3-month committed buffer, run benchmark during private staging, Redwood to provide updated pricing and security artifacts.
action_items: Priya: Share updated 12-month renewal pricing with 3-month pilot option by 2026-12-02
Marco: Schedule 2-hour staging benchmark session (private VPC) and share runbook by 2026-12-06
Rae: Send list of compliance questions (SOC2/ISO scope) to Redwood by 2026-11-30
Tomás: Provide current traffic profile and 95th percentile latency targets by 2026-11-29
next_steps: Set up private VPC pilot and staging benchmark (Marco)
Confirm renewal commitment and PO window (Dana)
Follow-up call in two weeks to review benchmark results and finalize contract amendment
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-26 15:00 UTC | Duration 58 mins | Attendees: Priya Desai (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood CSM); Dana Li (Silvermist VP Eng), Tomás Ortega (Platform Lead), Rae Hsu (Security), Elliott Grant (SRE)

[00:00] Priya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. we've got 58 minutes on the calendar — agenda is renewal timeline, capacity uplift, and the EU onboarding pilot. quick intros?
[00:12] Dana: hey, Dana here. we'll be making a decision by early December ideally.
[00:16] Tomás: Tomás — platform lead — we'll be hands on for the staging run.
[00:21] Rae: Rae, security. quick note: SOC two material and SAML integration are blockers for procurement.
[00:28] Priya: totally understood. Marco, quick intro?
[00:31] Marco: hi all, Marco Ruiz, I'm the SE, I'll own benchmarks and the private vpc plan.
[00:36] Priya: great. first — renewal posture. Dana, where are you in terms of what you need to sign off?
[00:44] Dana: timeline wise, product wants continuity; legal needs contract terms cleared. we're looking at a modest committed uplift — roughly 25% more tokens than current — plus a burst pool for unpredictable spikes. cost is a factor so we wanted to talk tradeoffs.
[00:58] Priya: ok makes sense. on Redwood side we've got two levers — dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) and on-demand burst. dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost efficiency; burst covers sudden spikes. Marco, can you speak to latency implications?
[01:10] Marco: yeah so dedicated with proper batching hits our low 90s ms median on the models you're using; burst on shared infra can be a bit more variable, maybe 180–350 ms p95 depending on load. quantization and batching configs can shift that.
[01:28] Tomás: p95 350ms is on the high side for us — customer-facing inference needs <250 p95. is that achievable on dedicated?
[01:35] Marco: with dedicated and prefix cache warmed, yes. also we can pin a lower-L memory quantized variant but that might affect quality slightly.
[01:44] Rae: and security — if we go dedicated on hosted, what are the guarantees on data separation? audit logs? KMS integration?
[01:52] Priya: we can do Dedicated capacity with customer isolation. for hosted dedicated we provide audit logs and KMS integration via our enterprise plan; private deployment (VPC) gives you full network isolation and customer-managed keys if you need HSM. we'll share the security binder after this.
[02:05] Rae: do you have SOC2 report and ISO statement available?
[02:09] Priya: yes, SOC2 Type II is available. I'll attach the report. Marco, can you add the logging doc link?
[02:15] Marco: sure — (link shared in chat) Redwood security binder / audit logs doc — note the retention windows vary by tier.
[02:22] Elliott: one quick ops question — what's the failover story if eu capacity drops? we have strict SLA requirements for EU customers.
[02:29] Priya: smart routing can failover to another region or to a lower-cost model variant; for SLAs we recommend Dedicated in EU plus cross-region fallback to US-W if required in the short term.
[02:40] Dana: what's the lead time to stand up EU dedicated nodes?
[02:42] Marco: 6–8 weeks typical for reserved capacity provisioning in a new region; can be faster with burst and initial private pilot.
[02:49] Dana: ok that's doable. legal wants an end date alignment — can you model a 12-month renewal with a 3-month pilot buffer?
[02:57] Priya: yes — we can propose 12-month commitment with an initial 3-month committed buffer (lower committed capacity) that transitions to full commit after the pilot. we'll include pricing bands.
[03:08] Tomás: for the pilot we need a runbook and a benchmark plan — we'll want to simulate production traffic and run token-level latency/cost breakdowns.
[03:17] Marco: understood. suggested plan: 2-hour staging benchmark in your private VPC; we'll capture p50/p95, token cost, and KV cache hit rates. I'll deliver the runbook and a sample data generator.
[03:29] Rae: logging and audit — can we get syslog/ELK or do you support raw event export?
[03:34] Marco: we support structured audit logs pushed to a customer log sink (S3/ELK) and can export traces. retention by tier.
[03:40] Rae: ok need to confirm retention window and where the keys are stored.
[03:44] Priya: KMS integration is via customer-managed keys on Private; on hosted dedicated we use our KMS but offer envelope encryption and key rotation options.
[03:54] Dana: cost — if we do dedicated EU plus burst, what's the delta vs current spend? rough numbers are fine.
[04:00] Priya: rough calc — given your current throughput and expected 25% uplift, dedicated increases committed cost ~+28% but reduces per-token variance; burst pool is billed differently (peak-based). I'll send an updated pricing illustrative spreadsheet.
[04:13] Tomás: can we get sample numbers for the model variants — e.g., base float32 vs 4-bit quantized?
[04:18] Marco: yes — float32 is fastest for quality but costliest; 4-bit quant drops cost by ~45–60% depending on model and may add ~3–6% latency improvement. quality delta depends on model and prompts. we'll include eval guidance.
[04:33] (00:04:35) Dana: there's occasional confusion in our stack about KV cache eviction — is there an interface for cache metrics?
[04:40] Marco: yes, metrics for cache hit rate and TTL. our ops api exposes them.
[04:44] Elliott: can we run a 24 hour soak test? realistic traffic pattern?
[04:48] Marco: yes — for staging we recommend a 24–72 hour soak, but 24 hours should be sufficient for initial peak behavior.
[04:54] Rae: procurement is asking about indemnity and data residency clauses for EU — any legal templates?
[05:00] Priya: we have standard clauses and can share a redline-friendly contract; for EU residency we can host in eu-west and sign a data processing addendum.
[05:08] Tomás: on the technical side, what's the network latency expectation inside the VPC? we host part of our services in eu-west-1.
[05:15] Marco: intra-region network latency is sub 10–20ms. model inference latency is the dominant factor.
[05:20] Dana: ok. let's talk numbers and timelines to align on next steps.
[05:25] Priya: action items — I'll summarize but Marco will schedule the benchmark. we propose: 1) price + contract options 2) security binder and SOC2 3) staging runbook + benchmark 4) follow-up in two weeks.
[05:37] (00:05:38) Dana: does Redwood support SSO — SAML/SCIM for our user provisioning?
[05:42] Priya: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning on enterprise plans.
[05:46] Rae: for audit we also want IP allow-listing and role-based access controls.
[05:50] Marco: RBAC supported; IP allow-listing on private deployments and certain dedicated plans.
[05:56] Tomás: if we need private on-prem later, what's the migration path?
[06:00] Priya: we have a private deployment package; migration typically involves model artifacts + config sync, takes several weeks with our ops team. we'll add a migration whitepaper.
[06:10] Dana: curious about throttling — can Redwood enforce per-route quotas and graceful degradation?
[06:15] Marco: yes per-route throttles, auto-fallback to a lower-cost model variant, and circuit-breaker style policies.
[06:21] Elliott: also want token-level billing breakdowns per route.
[06:24] Priya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns per token and per route.
[06:29] Dana: good. procurement will ask for the PO window; can you support a 30-day PO?
[06:34] Priya: yes standard is 30 days; we can accommodate.
[06:37] (00:06:38) Rae: any known vendor security gaps we should flag?
[06:41] Marco: we don't currently support customer-managed HSM in hosted dedicated — it's available in private with HSM integrations. we'll note that.
[06:47] Rae: noted.
[06:49] Priya: ok let's outline the pilot and pricing. proposed: 3-month pilot with modest committed buffer (50% of requested uplift) in EU dedicated staging, with burst enabled and a follow-on amendment to convert to full 12-month commit after successful benchmark.
[07:05] Dana: acceptable if benchmarks meet p95 <250 and cost within thresholds.
[07:10] Tomás: will the benchmark capture KV cache warm start effects?
[07:14] Marco: yes we'll run cold and warm cache passes and show hit-rate impact.
[07:18] Priya: timeline: Priya sends pricing + contract draft by end of week (Dec 2). Marco schedules benchmark and runbook by Dec 6. Customer returns compliance Qs by Nov 30. follow-up call week of Dec 7.
[07:32] (00:07:33) Dana: any final questions?
[07:36] Rae: just one — do you support step-scaling for dedicated pools?
[07:40] Marco: yes we have autoscale policies and manual step-scaling; burst covers sudden unexpected increases.
[07:46] Elliott: good.
[07:47] Priya: i'll send a recap and the security binder after this meeting. thanks everyone.
[07:53] Tomás: thanks.
[07:55] Dana: appreciate it.

[00:30:00 section – long form notes omitted for brevity]

[30:01] (00:30:02) Marco: diving deeper — sample benchmark plan: create synthetic load mirroring your RPS profile (attached later), run 2hr mixed traffic, measure token latency distribution, cost per 1M tokens, cache hit rate, and scaling delta.
[30:20] Tomás: can Redwood provide sample traffic generator?
[30:22] Marco: yes will provide a small GH repo and a set of JMX-style scripts; we'll also send a spreadsheet to map your route names to token buckets.
[30:30] Rae: security — will logs include user identifiers? we need pseudonymization for EU PII flows.
[30:35] Marco: logs can be configured to mask PII; for any PII we recommend tokenization at ingress.
[30:41] Dana: ok, that's helpful.

[00:45:00 approx — final recap]
[45:02] Priya: recap and owners: Priya to send pricing + SOC2 + contract redline template by 2026-12-02; Marco to share runbook and schedule pilot by 2026-12-06; Rae to send compliance Qs by 2026-11-30; Tomás to share traffic profile by 2026-11-29. We'll reconvene two weeks after the benchmark to finalize amendment.
[45:30] Dana: that's good, thanks.
[45:34] Priya: great, meeting adjourned.

(End of transcript)
